Knowledge.title: Calling Non-Static Methods
Knowledge.statement: Calling a non-static method requires an object and the dot notation: objectName.methodName(). The parentheses are mandatory even when the method takes no parameters.

Knowledge.title: String is an object type
Knowledge.statement: In Java, a String is an object type, not a primitive, so it is stored and manipulated via references to String objects.

TeachingStep.title: OO Motivation
TeachingStep.statement: Opens by framing why object-oriented programming matters and sketches how a program is a collection of interacting objects.

Knowledge.title: What Is an Object
Knowledge.statement: An object in an object-oriented program is any thing that can be a physical item or a mental construct; it is modeled with its own state (attributes) and behavior (methods).

Knowledge.title: Design Recipe Components
Knowledge.statement: The Design Recipe consists of four main elements: data definitions, method signatures with purpose statements, examples with tests, and a skeleton or method template. Each element guides a different stage of program design.

Knowledge.title: Class Hierarchy
Knowledge.statement: Classes group objects into types; a class is a blueprint that defines common attributes and behaviors shared by all instances of that type.

Knowledge.title: Generic Box Class Declaration
Knowledge.statement: Declare a public generic class Box<T> that stores a value of type T in a private field and exposes public set(T) and get() methods; demonstrate usage by showing Box<String> as an example.

TeachingStep.title: Intro to While Loops
TeachingStep.statement: Introduces the concept of a while loop and explains that it repeats a block of statements as long as a boolean condition remains true.

TeachingStep.title: While Loop Semantics
TeachingStep.statement: Defines the semantics of a while loop: it executes the body while the condition is true, and exits when the condition becomes false.

TeachingStep.title: While vs If
TeachingStep.statement: Compares while loops to if statements, highlighting that while can repeat, whereas an if executes once.

TeachingStep.title: Three Steps to Writing a Loop
TeachingStep.statement: Presents the three steps to writing a loop: initialize the loop variable, test it in the loop condition, and update it inside the body.

TeachingStep.title: Tracing Loops Intro
TeachingStep.statement: Introduces the Tracing Loops section and the practice of tracing variable values each iteration to predict loop behavior.

TeachingStep.title: Common Errors with Loops
TeachingStep.statement: Introduces common errors with loops, including infinite loops and off-by-one errors, and how to avoid them.

TeachingStep.title: Input-Controlled Loops
TeachingStep.statement: Introduces input-controlled loops and the idea of a sentinel value to stop the loop.

TeachingStep.title: Loop Summary
TeachingStep.statement: Summarizes key concepts: loop control variable, when the boolean is evaluated, and typical loop problems like infinite or off-by-one errors.

Knowledge.title: Step 0 role in Design Recipe
Knowledge.statement: Step 0 is the prerequisite to the rest of the Design Recipe: understand and restate the problem before coding. Restating clarifies data definitions, constraints, and success criteria so subsequent steps build on the right problem.

Knowledge.title: String Immutability
Knowledge.statement: Java Strings are immutable: methods like toUpperCase() or substring() return new String objects, leaving the original unchanged.

Knowledge.title: Equals vs. ==
Knowledge.statement: For string content comparison, use .equals(...) rather than ==, because == checks reference identity and may not reflect identical text.

Knowledge.title: Length and indexing
Knowledge.statement: length() returns the number of characters in the string; charAt(index) returns the character at the specified index, with bounds checking to avoid errors.

Knowledge.title: String Literals and String Pool
Knowledge.statement: String literals may be interned in the string pool; new String("x") creates a distinct object outside the pool.

Knowledge.title: Design Recipe for Strings
Knowledge.statement: The Design Recipe framing (data definition, signatures, examples, skeleton, implementation) applies to string tasks like length, equality, or substring, guiding a step-by-step approach.

Knowledge.title: A: Equality Content Assessment
Knowledge.statement: Assessment: Explain why 's1 == s2' may be incorrect for string content equality and how '.equals()' addresses this.

TeachingStep.title: Intro: Strings Overview
TeachingStep.statement: Opens with an overview of Strings in Java, emphasizing that strings are objects with immutable behavior and that they will be studied through the Design Recipe.
TeachingStep.rationale: Opens with overview of Strings and Design Recipe motivations.

TeachingStep.title: Strings as Objects
TeachingStep.statement: Strings in Java are objects, not primitive types; a String variable holds a reference to a String object.
TeachingStep.rationale: Introduce Strings as objects and the core properties to build intuition.

TeachingStep.title: Immutability of Strings
TeachingStep.statement: Java Strings are immutable: operations produce new String objects instead of modifying the original.
TeachingStep.rationale: Build intuition about immutability and references.

TeachingStep.title: Equals vs Equals: Identity vs Content
TeachingStep.statement: Introduce the distinction between object identity (==) and content equality (.equals) for Strings.

TeachingStep.title: Substring Intro
TeachingStep.statement: Substring is defined by beginIndex inclusive and endIndex exclusive; illustrate with simple examples.
TeachingStep.rationale: Prepare learners for substring task by presenting its key boundary semantics.

TeachingStep.title: IndexOf Intro
TeachingStep.statement: Overview of indexOf/lastIndexOf as string search utilities and their basic semantics.
TeachingStep.rationale: Lay groundwork for string search operations.

TeachingStep.title: Inspect Intro
TeachingStep.statement: Introduce Java String inspection concepts (length, isEmpty, charAt) in the context of a simple example.
TeachingStep.rationale: Motivate inspection tasks with practical scenarios.

TeachingStep.title: Strings Consolidation
TeachingStep.statement: Consolidate the core ideas: Strings are objects, immutable, and compared by content using equals, not by reference with ==.

TeachingStep.title: Motivation for Abstract Classes
TeachingStep.statement: Abstract classes provide blueprints for shared structure and behavior, enabling clearer designs and easier extension by subclasses.

TeachingStep.title: Motivation for Inheritance Design
TeachingStep.statement: Class inheritance helps organize related objects and supports the DRY principle by enabling shared behavior to be defined once and reused across a family of subclasses.

TeachingStep.title: Step 0: Understand & Restate with Inheritance in Mind
TeachingStep.statement: Step 0 invites you to understand and restate the problem with inheritance in mind, identifying recurring requirements that suggest a superclass.

TeachingStep.title: Step 1: Data Definitions & Inheritance-Aware Design
TeachingStep.statement: Step 1 emphasizes documenting shared vs. specialized data to reveal inheritance opportunities and guide the design of a class hierarchy.

TeachingStep.title: Step 2: Method Signatures & Purpose in Inheritance
TeachingStep.statement: Step 2 outlines specifying shared method signatures at the superclass and planning subclass overrides to align with the hierarchy.

TeachingStep.title: Iteration and Refinement of Hierarchy
TeachingStep.statement: Iterative refinement is a natural and valuable pattern: as you learn more, you refine your hierarchy to move shared functionality up the chain and adjust structure accordingly.

TeachingStep.title: DRY and Inheritance for Reusability
TeachingStep.statement: DRY principle motivates consolidating shared fields and methods in superclasses and using intermediate abstractions to reduce duplication.

TeachingStep.title: Chapter Conclusion: Inheritance in Design
TeachingStep.statement: Conclusion: inheritance planning aids DRY, design contracts, and emphasizes when to use interfaces for cross-cutting concerns.

TeachingStep.title: Integrated Inheritance Example
TeachingStep.statement: Integrated example of a social media post hierarchy showing Post, MediaPost, TextPost, PhotoPost, VideoPost with constructor chaining and polymorphism.

Knowledge.title: Class Blueprint
Knowledge.statement: A class is a blueprint that defines a family of objects by listing their common attributes and behaviors.

Knowledge.title: Method Header Structure
Knowledge.statement: A Java method header consists of an access modifier (optional), an optional static keyword, a return type, a method name, and a parameter list in parentheses, followed by a body enclosed in braces. The header is typically followed by a body that defines the method's behavior.

TeachingStep.title: Exceptions Intro Motivation
TeachingStep.statement: Opens with a real-world example showing how silent sentinel values can cause incorrect results and motivates the need for structured error handling via exceptions.

TeachingStep.title: Java Exceptions Overview
TeachingStep.statement: Introduces the taxonomy of standard library exceptions (Errors, Checked Exceptions, Unchecked Exceptions) and explains how the compiler enforces some of them, setting expectations for error handling in code.

TeachingStep.title: Interfaces Intro Motivation
TeachingStep.statement: Motivates why interfaces matter by framing them as contracts that ensure consistent method names across classes.

TeachingStep.title: Interface Syntax Idea
TeachingStep.statement: Introduces interface syntax: declaring a public abstract method signature; explains that implementing classes must provide concrete methods.

TeachingStep.title: Interface Implementation Idea
TeachingStep.statement: Demonstrates implementing an interface with 'implements', and highlights the compile-time check that requires all methods to be defined.

TeachingStep.title: Interfaces Polymorphism Use
TeachingStep.statement: Demonstrates polymorphic usage by treating different implementations as the same type and invoking common methods.

TeachingStep.title: Interfaces Design Recipe Concept
TeachingStep.statement: Connects interface design to the design recipe steps, clarifying how data definitions, contracts, tests, and skeletons map to interface design.

TeachingStep.title: Interfaces Mistakes Overview
TeachingStep.statement: Summarizes common mistakes when using interfaces and outlines best practices to avoid them.

Knowledge.title: Object ID
Knowledge.statement: An object's id is the name by which it is referred to in the program.

Knowledge.title: Pre-implementation Testing Plan
Knowledge.statement: Write a small table of representative examples and edge cases before coding. This anchors what counts as correct behavior and reduces guesswork during implementation.

Knowledge.title: Reflection Prompts after Design Steps
Knowledge.statement: Embed reflection prompts after key steps to enable self-assessment and learning. For example, ask what would have happened without a precondition and how edge cases were surfaced during design.

Knowledge.title: Boundary-first Debugging Heuristic
Knowledge.statement: Adopt debugging heuristics that prioritize boundary and index checks when tests fail. This focus often isolates off-by-one and range errors quickly.

Knowledge.title: Test Table Design Before Coding
Knowledge.statement: Use explicit test tables to enumerate inputs, expected outputs, and edge cases before writing code. This aligns with the Design Recipe and reduces ambiguity in implementation.

Knowledge.title: UML Diagrams
Knowledge.statement: UML diagrams are a standard visual notation for depicting objects, their attributes, and their interactions.

Knowledge.title: Pause Before Coding
Knowledge.statement: Pause before coding to plan your data design. Ask: What data do I have? Where do these fields come from? What constraints apply? How might the data evolve over time? This metacognitive habit helps prevent brittle code by surfacing assumptions before implementation.

Knowledge.title: Design Recipe in Practice
Knowledge.statement: Design Recipe provides a disciplined, step-by-step workflow for solving programming problems: restate the problem, define the data, write tests, scaffold a solution, implement, and reflect on the result.

Knowledge.title: Reflection Prompts for Revision
Knowledge.statement: Reflection prompts guide post-implementation thinking: question assumptions, compare actual results to expectations, and consider what changes would improve the design or extend the solution.

Knowledge.title: Testing Plan Before Code
Knowledge.statement: Plan tests before coding by enumerating edge cases and expected behaviors, ensuring tests cover critical paths and boundary conditions.

Knowledge.title: Iterative Design Mindset
Knowledge.statement: Iterative design involves starting with a minimal skeleton, then incrementally filling in details, validating with tests, and refining as requirements clarify.

Knowledge.title: Edge-Case First Approach
Knowledge.statement: Always consider boundary conditions and empty inputs early; explicitly design tests for these cases to prevent surprises in real usage.

Knowledge.title: Debugging Heuristics for Test Failures
Knowledge.statement: Adopt debugging heuristics: when tests fail, first check boundary conditions and inputs, then verify API contracts and data state before diving deeper.

TeachingStep.title: Objects and Classes Intro
TeachingStep.statement: This section introduces Objects and Classes and motivates the idea of modeling real-world entities using classes. It defines key terms like object, class, attributes, and methods.

TeachingStep.title: Classes as Blueprints
TeachingStep.statement: A class defines a new data type or blueprint for objects; objects are created as instances of that class.

TeachingStep.title: Attributes and Behaviors of Objects
TeachingStep.statement: Objects have attributes (data) and behaviors (methods); attributes are stored as instance variables and behaviors as methods.

TeachingStep.title: Objects/Classes in Examples
TeachingStep.statement: The text uses examples such as the String class, Person, Dog, etc. to illustrate objects and classes.

TeachingStep.title: Practice Introduction
TeachingStep.statement: Practice exercises in the Practice subsection reinforce the definitions through drag-and-drop matching and multiple-choice questions.

Knowledge.title: Objects Interact via Messages
Knowledge.statement: Objects interact by sending messages to each other, which may trigger actions and changes in state.

Knowledge.title: Inheritance opportunity identification
Knowledge.statement: Identify shared attributes and behaviors across related classes (e.g., TextPost, PhotoPost, VideoPost) and plan a superclass or interface before implementing details, thereby recognizing opportunities for inheritance early in the design process.

Knowledge.title: Inheritance planning in Design Recipe steps
Knowledge.statement: Integrate class hierarchy planning into Steps 0–2 of the Design Recipe to identify shared structures early and guide the data definitions toward a coherent superclass/interface.

Knowledge.title: Override rules for subclass methods
Knowledge.statement: Design method signatures with clear rules for overriding in subclasses: specify which methods must be overridden, which may be overridden, and which must not override core invariants.

Knowledge.title: Iterative refinement in inheritance design
Knowledge.statement: Apply iterative refinement to improve class hierarchies: reassess and prune the design as you identify shared attributes and test inheritance assumptions.

Knowledge.title: DRY principle in inheritance design
Knowledge.statement: Apply the DRY principle to reduce duplication by extracting shared fields and behaviors into a superclass or interface, then propagate those definitions to subclasses.

Knowledge.title: Avoiding retrofitting costs in inheritance design
Knowledge.statement: Address the cost of retrofitting inheritance by identifying shared functionality early and outlining a plan to extract common elements before coding, to avoid expensive refactoring later.

Knowledge.title: Worked example: shared post attributes
Knowledge.statement: Worked example: TextPost, PhotoPost, and VideoPost share fields author, timestamp, and likes; consolidating these into a common superclass reduces duplication and simplifies maintenance.

Knowledge.title: Minimal Java Program
Knowledge.statement: A minimal Java program must declare a public class and provide a main method as the program entry point.

Knowledge.title: Plan Before Implementing
Knowledge.statement: Before coding, outline a plan using a lightweight design recipe: restate the problem, define data types, specify the API, and sketch boundary-test cases. This planning step anchors learning and reduces detours.

Knowledge.title: For loop syntax
Knowledge.statement: A for loop controls iteration by three parts: initialization of the loop counter, a termination condition, and an update expression executed after each iteration.

Knowledge.title: While loop syntax
Knowledge.statement: A while loop repeats its body as long as the condition evaluates to true; the condition is checked before each iteration.

Knowledge.title: Do-while loop syntax
Knowledge.statement: A do-while loop executes the body at least once, then repeats while the condition is true; the condition is evaluated after the loop body.

Knowledge.title: For-each loop syntax
Knowledge.statement: A for-each loop iterates over elements in a collection without explicit index management; syntax varies by language but typically uses an element variable and a collection.

Knowledge.title: Constructing an iterable from an array
Knowledge.statement: Arrays or arrays-like collections can be traversed by creating an Iterable or using a for-each over the collection; this often involves wrapping the array or using framework utilities.

Knowledge.title: Iteration mastery
Knowledge.statement: Learners can correctly choose and apply appropriate loop constructs (for, while, do-while, for-each) to traverse data structures.

writes correct loop headers with proper termination conditions
explains edge cases such as empty collections

Knowledge.title: Iterable construction mastery
Knowledge.statement: Learners can construct and use an iterable from arrays/collections and apply for-each traversal correctly.
rubric_criteria: constructs an iterable from an array
uses for-each with proper element type and variable names

Knowledge.title: For-loop summation exercise
Knowledge.statement: Write a function that sums elements of an int[] using a for loop with an index variable and returns the total.

Knowledge.title: Iterable construction exercise
Knowledge.statement: Provide an array and ask students to construct an iterable and perform an action using for-each or an iterator.

Knowledge.title: Mutator methods definition
Knowledge.statement: Mutator methods are public void methods that change the value of an instance variable (or static variable) and do not return a value.

Knowledge.title: Print Commands
Knowledge.statement: To print output in Java, use System.out.print or System.out.println for values followed by a newline, respectively.

Knowledge.title: Class Relationships
Knowledge.statement: Classes can be related through inheritance, composition, and association, forming a hierarchy and networks of types and objects.

Knowledge.title: Update Rating Signature
Knowledge.statement: The function signature for updating a rating is def update_rating(library: list, song_title: str, new_rating: int) -> bool, which declares the inputs and return type.

Knowledge.title: Mutator method pattern
Knowledge.statement: Write a mutator method: make it public, return void, name it setX with parameter of the new value and assign the value to the corresponding field.

Knowledge.title: First Java Program Template
Knowledge.statement: A Java program begins with a public class definition and a main method as the program entry point.

Knowledge.title: Interface declaration
Knowledge.statement: Declare an interface using the 'interface' keyword; the interface name should be capitalized and used to specify a contract of methods without bodies.

Knowledge.title: Step 0 problem restated
Knowledge.statement: Step 0 is a planning practice: understand and restate the problem before coding, so the team shares a clear target and success criteria for the solution.

Knowledge.title: Abstract Class Definition
Knowledge.statement: An abstract class in Java cannot be instantiated directly; it serves as a blueprint for subclasses that provide implementations for abstract methods.

Knowledge.title: Abstract Class Blueprint
Knowledge.statement: An abstract class defines a partial contract: it may hold shared state and concrete methods, but requires subclasses to implement abstract methods; it serves as a blueprint for an inheritance hierarchy.

Knowledge.title: Abstract Class Instantiation Rule
Knowledge.statement: An abstract class cannot be instantiated; you cannot create objects from it using new, reinforcing its role as a template for subclasses.

Knowledge.title: Blueprint vs Template in Inheritance
Knowledge.statement: Abstract classes act as blueprints or templates for a family of concrete subclasses, shaping common structure while leaving concrete details to subclasses.

Knowledge.title: Interface Contract Definition
Knowledge.statement: An interface is a pure contract that declares methods a class must implement, without providing concrete implementations or per-instance state outside of constants.

Knowledge.title: Interface Characteristics
Knowledge.statement: Interfaces cannot store per-instance state (no instance fields) and are used to declare capabilities that may be implemented by unrelated classes.

Knowledge.title: Interface Instantiation Restriction
Knowledge.statement: Interfaces cannot be instantiated; they define a contract that concrete classes implement.

Knowledge.title: Interface Default Methods
Knowledge.statement: Since Java 8, interfaces may include default methods with implementations, enabling evolution of interfaces without breaking existing implementations.

Knowledge.title: Abstract Class vs Interface Contrast
Knowledge.statement: Abstract classes support a mix of abstract and concrete methods and may hold state, whereas interfaces define a contract with no per-instance state (except constants) and can include default methods since Java 8.

Knowledge.title: When to Use Interfaces in Inheritance Guidelines
Knowledge.statement: Use interfaces to model cross-cutting capabilities rather than forcing unrelated classes into a single inheritance hierarchy.

Knowledge.title: DRY Principle in Inheritance Design
Knowledge.statement: Inheritance design should consider DRY principles, promoting reuse and reducing duplication through carefully planned hierarchies.

Knowledge.title: Step 1 Data Definitions Inheritance
Knowledge.statement: Step 1 (Data Definitions) organizes shared vs. specialized attributes and invariants into a hierarchy, highlighting potential superclasses (e.g., a Post superclass with common fields).

Knowledge.title: Step 2 Data Step Method Signatures Inheritance
Knowledge.statement: Step 2 (Method Signatures) identifies shared methods in the superclass for inheritance, and outlines how subclass overrides may be declared or implemented.

Knowledge.title: Iterative Refinement in Inheritance
Knowledge.statement: Inheritance hierarchies can be refined iteratively across steps 0–2 as new shared attributes are discovered, enabling gradual improvements rather than big redesigns.

Knowledge.title: DRY Principle in Inheritance (General)
Knowledge.statement: The DRY principle is central to inheritance design: avoid duplicating the same code or invariants across multiple subclasses by moving them up to a common superclass or intermediate class.

Knowledge.title: Post Shared Fields Definition
Knowledge.statement: Post superclass defines shared fields (author, timestamp, likeCount, comments) that concrete post types inherit.

Knowledge.title: MediaPost Hierarchy Definition
Knowledge.statement: MediaPost intermediate superclass captures media-related attributes (fileSize, resolution) shared by PhotoPost and VideoPost.

Knowledge.title: TextPost Data Definition
Knowledge.statement: TextPost specializes Post with textContent and wordCount fields.

Knowledge.title: PhotoPost Data Definition
Knowledge.statement: PhotoPost extends MediaPost with imageFile and caption fields.

Knowledge.title: VideoPost Data Definition
Knowledge.statement: VideoPost extends MediaPost with videoFile, description, and duration fields.

Knowledge.title: Integrated Inheritance Strategy
Knowledge.statement: Inheritance design integrates inheritance planning, DRY, and cross-cutting concerns (interfaces) to create a cohesive design strategy.

Knowledge.title: Metacognitive Contracts: Living Docs and Planning
Knowledge.statement: Treat function contracts as living documentation that guides planning, reflection, and verification. Writing a clear signature and purpose statement clarifies which inputs are valid, what the function promises to do, and how to recognize when it has changed, enabling learners to monitor progress and plan tests accordingly.

Knowledge.title: Data Field Definition
Knowledge.statement: A data definition specifies the fields that make up a data type and the constraints that apply to each field.

Knowledge.title: Data Blueprint (Concept)
Knowledge.statement: A data definition acts as a blueprint for organizing and using data throughout a program, clarifying what data must look like.

Knowledge.title: Function Contract Structure
Knowledge.statement: A function contract typically lists preconditions, input types, the return value, and potential error cases.

Knowledge.title: Function Contract Components
Knowledge.statement: The four components of a function contract are preconditions, input types, return value, and error cases.

Knowledge.title: Draft Informal Function Contract
Knowledge.statement: Draft an informal contract for a function described in the scenario, including a signature, a purpose statement, and a list of preconditions.

Knowledge.title: Time.tick edge example
Knowledge.statement: Edge case demonstration: tick() on 23:59:59 yields 00:00:00.

Knowledge.title: Time.add method
Knowledge.statement: The add(Time offset) method adds the offset to the current time, carrying over seconds to minutes and minutes to hours, and wrapping hours at 24.

Knowledge.title: Time.add typical example
Knowledge.statement: Example: Time(1,1,1).add(Time(2,2,2)) yields 03:03:03.

Knowledge.title: Time.add edge example
Knowledge.statement: Edge: Time(23,59,59).add(Time(0,0,1)) yields 00:00:00.

Knowledge.title: StepTracker instance variables
Knowledge.statement: Identify and declare the StepTracker instance variables needed to track the minimum steps, total steps, number of days, and number of active days.

Knowledge.title: StepTracker activeDays

Knowledge.title: StepTracker addDailySteps
Knowledge.statement: Implement addDailySteps(int steps) to accumulate daily steps, update total and possibly increment active days when the daily total crosses the threshold.

Knowledge.title: StepTracker averageSteps
Knowledge.statement: Implement averageSteps() to return the total steps divided by days tracked (double), returning 0.0 if no days tracked.

Knowledge.title: StepTracker addDailySteps typical example

Knowledge.statement: Example: after a sequence with 1 active day and total 13000 steps, average=13000.0.

Knowledge.statement: Overload the talk method by adding a parameter String name to print Hello <name> instead of the original Hello.

Knowledge.title: update_rating skeleton
Knowledge.statement: Implementation of update_rating follows the Design Recipe steps: validate inputs, search for the target song by title, update the rating, and return a boolean indicating success.

Knowledge.title: Compile and Run Flow
Knowledge.statement: Code execution in a Java program follows: compile, then run starting at main method; compile errors block execution.

Knowledge.title: Method Signature Definition
Knowledge.statement: A function's method signature communicates how to call it: it states the function name and its parameters, and, in languages like Python, the return type as part of the signature.

Knowledge.title: Purpose Statement Concept
Knowledge.statement: A purpose statement explains what a function does and doesn't do.

Knowledge.title: Preconditions Definition
Knowledge.statement: Preconditions specify the conditions that must hold about inputs before a function runs.

Knowledge.title: Input Types Definition
Knowledge.statement: Input types describe what kind of data each parameter accepts.

Knowledge.title: Return Value Definition
Knowledge.statement: Return value describes what the function outputs on a successful call or, more generally, what a function promises to yield.

Knowledge.title: Error Cases Definition
Knowledge.statement: Error cases describe how a function responds to invalid inputs or violated preconditions.

Knowledge.title: Type Hints in Signatures
Knowledge.statement: Type hints in Python signatures indicate expected parameter types and the return type.

Knowledge.title: Living Documentation of Contracts
Knowledge.statement: Function contracts serve as living documentation that stays in sync with the code and guide testing.

Knowledge.title: Design Recipe Workflow
Knowledge.statement: The Design Recipe workflow emphasizes a disciplined progression: data definitions; signature and purpose; skeleton; full implementation; tests; and refinement.

Knowledge.title: Variable Declaration Scope
Knowledge.statement: Declare variables with appropriate types and scope within methods; variables must be defined within a method or block.

Knowledge.title: Compute popularity formula
Knowledge.statement: The compute_popularity function is defined as rating * log(play_count + 1).

Knowledge.title: Semicolon Rule
Knowledge.statement: Java statements end with semicolons; capitalization matters for System vs system, etc.

Knowledge.title: Abstract class components
Knowledge.statement: An abstract class in Java can declare fields, constructors, concrete methods, and abstract methods. Abstract methods are declared without a body and must be implemented by any concrete subclass.

Knowledge.title: Abstract method contract
Knowledge.statement: An abstract method is declared without an implementation and specifies the signature (name, parameters, return type). Subclasses must provide an implementation for all abstract methods to become concrete.

Knowledge.title: Subclass implements abstract methods
Knowledge.statement: A concrete subclass extends an abstract class and implements all abstract methods, typically by providing method bodies and using the @Override annotation.

Knowledge.title: Polymorphism with abstract classes
Knowledge.statement: Abstract classes enable polymorphism by allowing code to operate on the abstract superclass type, while concrete subclasses provide specific behavior.

Knowledge.title: Override annotation tip
Knowledge.statement: Using @Override when implementing abstract methods helps catch signature mismatches at compile time and improves readability.

Knowledge.title: Generic Box Usage Example
Knowledge.statement: Worked example: creating a Box<String>, calling set to store a String and get() to retrieve it, demonstrating how the type parameter T provides compile-time type safety.

Knowledge.title: Generic Methods: printArray Example
Knowledge.statement: Worked example: generic static method printArray<E>(E[] inputArray) prints elements of arrays of different types (Integer[], String[], Player[]), illustrating type inference for E.

Knowledge.title: Generic Methods: getFirstElement Example
Knowledge.statement: Worked example: generic method getFirstElement<List<T>>(List<T>) returning T, with examples using List<String> and List<Integer> to show type inference and return typing.

Knowledge.title: Wildcard: Unbounded List Demo
Knowledge.statement: Worked example: unbounded wildcard List<?> usage in a printAnyList method showing how you can read elements as Object but cannot add elements (except null) due to unknown type.

Knowledge.title: Diamond Operator Demo
Knowledge.statement: Worked example: use of the Diamond Operator <> for type inference in Box<String> example and Box<?> usage, illustrating concise generic instance creation.

Knowledge.title: compute_popularity skeleton
Knowledge.statement: Compute_popularity skeleton includes validating input, computing rating * log(play_count + 1), and returning the result.

Knowledge.title: Time rollover analogy
Knowledge.statement: An analogy between time rollover and time-keeping logic helps learners understand how a tick() method should advance time. The seconds wrap from 59 to 0 and increment minutes, minutes wrap from 59 to 0 and increment hours, and hours wrap from 23 to 0 as part of the clock behavior.

Knowledge.title: Debugging Flow
Knowledge.statement: Debugging is a normal part of coding; start by running code to observe failures and iterate fixes.

Knowledge.title: Design Recipe Confidence
Knowledge.statement: A disciplined Design Recipe process reduces late-debugging and promotes confidence in the final implementation.

Knowledge.title: Examples and Tests Purpose
Knowledge.statement: After clarifying a function's contract, you define concrete examples to illustrate expected behavior, then convert those examples into automated tests so checks can be repeated as the code evolves.

Knowledge.title: Java Inheritance Syntax
Knowledge.statement: To declare inheritance in Java, use the extends keyword in the class declaration. The subclass automatically inherits non-private members from the superclass and can add or override its own members.

Knowledge.title: Entity-Player Inheritance Example
Knowledge.statement: A complete inheritance example showing a base class Entity with health and takeDamage, and a subclass Player that adds experience points and leveling up. Demonstrates inherited fields/methods and extension.

Knowledge.title: Monster Inheritance Example
Knowledge.statement: Subclass Monster extends Entity to illustrate inheritance, showing how a subclass automatically gains non-private members from a superclass and can override or extend behavior as needed.

Knowledge.title: Override Annotation Demonstration

TeachingStep.title: Right-hand-side Expressions

Knowledge.title: Anatomy of a Java Class
Knowledge.statement: A Java class defines a new data type and serves as a blueprint for objects. An object is an instance of a class, created by new ClassName();, and the class body contains fields (instance variables) and methods.

Knowledge.title: Creating a Class
Knowledge.statement: Creating a Class: declare a class with public class Name { ... }. To create objects, use ClassName obj = new ClassName(); which calls a constructor in the class body.

Knowledge.title: Instance Variables
Knowledge.statement: Instance variables (fields) hold the data for an object. They are typically declared private to encapsulate data and accessed via methods inside the class.

Knowledge.title: Methods in a Class
Knowledge.statement: Methods define what an object can do. They are usually public; private methods are used for internal behavior. Methods can access instance variables within the class.

Knowledge.title: Constructor Structure
Knowledge.statement: Constructors have the same name as the class and no return type. They are used to initialize the object's instance variables when a new object is created.

Knowledge.title: Constructor Overloading
Knowledge.statement: Classes often have more than one constructor: a no-parameter constructor and a parameterized constructor to initialize all instance variables.

Knowledge.title: Default Constructor
Knowledge.statement: If you define at least one constructor, Java does not automatically provide a no-argument default constructor unless you explicitly define one.

Knowledge.title: Accessor Methods
Knowledge.statement: Accessor methods (getters) provide read access to private instance variables; they return the value and take no parameters.

Knowledge.title: Mutator Methods
Knowledge.statement: Mutator methods (setters) modify private instance variables and typically have a void return type and take a parameter to set the new value.

Knowledge.title: Static vs Instance
Knowledge.statement: Static variables and methods belong to the class itself, not to any particular object. They are accessed via ClassName.member and there is a single shared copy across all instances.

Knowledge.title: Scope and Access
Knowledge.statement: Scope defines where a variable is accessible. Class scope, method scope, and block scope determine visibility; private/public modifiers restrict external access.

Knowledge.title: This Keyword

Knowledge.title: Strings Basics

Knowledge.title: String Concatenation

Knowledge.statement: The double data type stores floating-point numbers (numbers with fractional parts).
